title: Multi-agent, cross-chat, and goal orchestration contract

referenceWalk.activity: A no-repository Multitask goal launched two read-only subagents in parallel and the parent synthesized their linked reports.
directlyObserved: Multitask can decompose one parent request into named asynchronous subagents.
Each subagent has an independent linked session UUID, model, effort, live status, transcript, stop control, and completion state.
The parent stays active, reports child progress, waits for results, and produces a final synthesis with child-session links.
Finished subagents expose their task prompt, transcript, files changed, review entry point, duration, model, and effort.
New chat offers prior-conversation search or summarization as context.
referenceWalk.verifiedLimit: Cursor past-chat references and @ mentions attach context; session IDs resume the same child. They are not a chat-to-chat delivery mailbox.

semantics.attachContext: Read or summarize a prior chat into the current agent without waking or modifying the source chat.
semantics.messageExistingChat: Deliver a peer turn to one existing live Workhorse chat, preserve sender and target identities, run that chat's assigned provider/model, and return its real reply.
semantics.spawnAgent: Dispatch a bounded child task; when the user did not explicitly assign provider, model, effort, or worker, leave them unset so Workhorse selects from task fit and capacity. Resume a compatible named or idle worker only when reuse rules allow it.
semantics.orchestrateGoal: Keep one parent responsible for an active goal, choose useful next work, delegate where justified, reconcile child evidence, and stop only at a real terminal state.
semantics.identityRule: Visible titles are convenient selectors; immutable Workhorse session IDs are the durable address and must be copyable, linkable, and never guessed.
semantics.truthRule: A context attachment is not a message, a resumed child is not a new agent, and a catalog or requested model is not runtime proof.
semantics.importPlan: Normalize Markdown into stable task ids, dependencies, acceptance checks, source hash, and awaiting-approval state without dispatch.
semantics.approvePlan: Approve one exact plan id, revision, and source hash before execution.
semantics.resumePlan: Continue the same plan and task attempts after pause or restart without dispatching completed work again.
semantics.workerReuse: A named or automatic follow-up may reuse only an idle, hidden, unarchived worker under the same parent and project with matching provider, model, effort, and custom connection; busy or incompatible work gets a distinct worker.
semantics.waveJoin: A completed worker wave wakes and joins its accountable parent exactly once; later waves can continue the same orchestration. When OpenClaw or Hermes owns the wave, Workhorse returns the reports to that harness and never starts a competing desk orchestration turn.
semantics.adaptiveMission: Ordinary delegation is one wave. An explicit adaptive loop preserves acceptance criteria, exclusions, evidence, pass lineage, and a bounded ceiling; a terminal incomplete pass may continue through workhorse_continue_mission, and each new pass returns to independent Workhorse routing. Required follow-up stays at the parent mission level; a leaf helper remains an optional bounded check whose failure returns remaining work to that parent.
semantics.budgetTruth: A token ceiling is enforced as work runs, not only labelled afterward. Crossing the verification reserve stops producing and requires a bounded handoff before the run can become budget-exceeded. Budget-exceeded is unsuccessful and reportless unless a truthful partial report was already recorded; a generic wave-finished notice never becomes child success or mission completion. An unset ceiling is unbounded. A reused worker does not inherit the previous slice’s ceiling or consumed count.
semantics.externalAgentSystem: OpenClaw and Hermes are discovered and called as permissioned harnesses, never providers, custom bots, usage rings, or bridge chats. Discovery is not permission: automatic routing requires Routing, Include harnesses, a selected agent, and one bounded plan grant; explicit named targets remain authoritative. An explicit request to work with Workhorse delegates through Workhorse before direct execution; a blocked delegation reports the exact Workhorse error before fallback. Each task supplies its task id, trace id, and explicit parent; dependent MCP orders preserve those fields. Inbound MCP is allowlisted; correlation rejects cycles, duplicate idempotency, and more than two hops.
semantics.planAdmission: Ordinary checklist evidence remains human-completable. An assigned builder step needs an independent read-only sibling auditor on another callable vendor; only a receipt with the worktree HEAD, named gate, final gate line, and pass status admits that builder step. The same receipt cannot complete an unassigned step. Elevate and vendor asks wait, while product asks on an active plan or goal state a recommendation and default before continuing.

cascadeLimits.model: Automatic children use the capacity-aware quick tier; explicit assignments win
cascadeLimits.effort: Derived from the selected quick route unless explicitly assigned
cascadeLimits.ordinaryLineupFanout: At most one worker per callable bot in a single ordinary lineup wave; the plan-specific root limit does not cap this roster fan-out.

automaticAssignmentMustExplain: why this agent or existing chat was selected
routingContract.fallbackRule: If the requested agent, skill, tool, provider capability, budget, capacity, or isolation is unavailable, stop or downgrade explicitly; never silently substitute identity or authority. Only installed skill references count as skills; free-form expertise is a capability.
routingContract.precedenceRule: An explicit child provider or model assignment wins unless it violates an inherited structured exclusion. Automatic nested routing defaults to quick, inherits exclusions, and records its capacity-aware decision.
routingContract.initialBrainRule: Harness delegation is fully automatic by default. An optional initial brain applies only to the first coordinating worker; unassigned descendants route independently.
routingContract.sequentialRule: Adaptive sequential work is opt-in per mission, never a global default. Every continuation names the exact prior worker ids and pass, preserves the mission contract, routes independently, and stops at complete, blocked, or its pass ceiling.
routingContract.selfRoutingRule: A plan task may choose its agent only after recording required capabilities, candidates, Watch state, cost, concurrency, isolation, and a short rationale.
routingContract.watchRule: A Watch-held provider receives no request. An approved capable fallback may run with the hold and substitution recorded.
routingContract.visualRule: Tasks tagged visual, UI, UX, image, or computer-use require the configured Kimi K3 visual profile unless the user overrides or accepts unavailability. Kimi is audit-only and hands implementation to a coding worker.
routingContract.effortRule: Choose the lowest sufficient supported reasoning effort for the task and record the rationale. Do not default every worker to high; explicit effort wins.
routingContract.skillRule: Critical installed skill identity, path, and required instructions survive context compaction.
routingContract.recoveryRule: On restart, reconcile orphaned running work to an explicit interrupted state, preserve elapsed time, release capacity, and continue eligible plan waves.
routingContract.reuseRule: Stable worker names are addressable. Compatible idle work can resume the same worker; busy, visible, archived, cross-parent, cross-project, or configuration-mismatched work cannot be silently reused.
